title: Invoice line-item mapping to telemetry (Hosted + Dedicated) — v1
author: Emily Stone
body:
## Purpose
This page is the canonical mapping between **invoice line items** (what Finance and customers see) and **telemetry-backed usage dimensions** (what Engineering and Analytics can query). It is used for:
- Invoice QA during close (pre-invoice checks + reconciliation sampling).
- Support/Sales explanations when customers report usage discrepancies.
- Experiment readouts where we segment revenue/usage by model family, region, endpoint type, and customer tier.

**Scope:** Hosted API meters + Dedicated usage attribution. (Private deployments are typically invoiced as platform/license + support; usage meters may be reported but are not the default invoice basis unless explicitly contracted.)

---

## Data sources and “source of truth”
**Primary billed-usage source of truth:** `billing_usage_aggregates` (billing-ready aggregates) produced from raw metering events.

**Telemetry sources used to explain/validate billed usage:**
1) Raw request logs (gateway/router): `inference_requests` (used for request counts, endpoint type, model routing context).
2) Metering events stream: `metering_events_v3` (token/units measured per request/stream segment).
3) Billing export snapshot (immutable per run): `invoice_usage_export` (what was used to generate invoice line items; includes `invoice_run_id`).

**Important:** When investigating a specific invoice, always pivot from the invoice to the immutable export for that run (by `invoice_run_id`) before comparing to “live” aggregates, because backfills and meter-version upgrades can change the live tables.

---

## Canonical dimensions (used across all mappings)
The following dimensions should be present (or derivable) for all usage-based line items:
- `customer_id` (billing account)
- `workspace_id` / `org_id` (product tenancy)
- `deployment_mode` (hosted | dedicated | private)
- `customer_tier` (self_serve | business | enterprise)
- `region` (canonical cloud region, e.g., `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`)
- `endpoint_type` (chat | completions | embeddings | rerank)
- `model_id` (canonical model identifier)
- `model_family` (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen)
- `model_alias` (commercial label shown in Console; may map many-to-one to `model_id` over time)
- `meter_name` and `meter_version` (see Hosted API meter dictionary)
- `aggregation_window_start` / `aggregation_window_end` (UTC)
- `invoice_run_id` (present in invoice export; used for auditability)

---

## Invoice line items → telemetry mapping (Hosted API)
Below, “Invoice line item name” refers to the human-readable line item on PDFs and in the billing portal. “Line item code” is what RevOps/Finance uses in exports.

### Table: Hosted API mapping
| Invoice line item name | Line item code | Meter name (billing) | Primary telemetry fields | Required filters/dimensions | Notes / customer-facing description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted API — Text generation: Input tokens | `HOSTED_TXT_INPUT_TOKENS` | `hosted.text.input_tokens` | `billed_input_tokens` from `billing_usage_aggregates` | `deployment_mode='hosted'` AND `endpoint_type IN ('chat','completions')` | Counts prompt + system + tool messages sent to the model. Excludes tokens served from prefix cache when `cached_input_tokens` is separately billed (see next line). |
| Hosted API — Text generation: Cached input tokens | `HOSTED_TXT_CACHED_INPUT_TOKENS` | `hosted.text.cached_input_tokens` | `cached_input_tokens` | Same as above + `cache_hit=true` in metering events | Only present for plans where cached tokens are itemized. If not itemized, cached tokens are included in input tokens and the line item is omitted. |
| Hosted API — Text generation: Output tokens | `HOSTED_TXT_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `hosted.text.output_tokens` | `billed_output_tokens` | `deployment_mode='hosted'` AND `endpoint_type IN ('chat','completions')` | Counts tokens generated and delivered to the client. For streaming: see ADR-027 and streaming notes below. |
| Hosted API — Embeddings units | `HOSTED_EMBEDDING_UNITS` | `hosted.embeddings.units` | `embedding_units` | `deployment_mode='hosted'` AND `endpoint_type='embeddings'` | One embedding unit corresponds to one input text/item embedded (not token-based). If customer uses batch inputs, units count equals number of items in the batch. |
| Hosted API — Rerank units | `HOSTED_RERANK_UNITS` | `hosted.rerank.units` | `rerank_units` | `deployment_mode='hosted'` AND `endpoint_type='rerank'` | One rerank unit corresponds to one query-document set processed. Exact definition (what constitutes a “document”) is in the meter dictionary. |
| Hosted API — Requests | `HOSTED_REQUESTS` | `hosted.requests` | `request_count` | `deployment_mode='hosted'` | Requests are itemized only on certain plans and are primarily used for rate-limit tiers and analytics. If present, it should reconcile to gateway request logs within tolerance after excluding auth failures and preflight. |

---

## Invoice line items → telemetry mapping (Dedicated)
Dedicated invoices typically have a **commit / reserved capacity component** plus (optional) **usage-based overage** depending on contract structure.

### Table: Dedicated mapping
| Invoice line item name | Line item code | Meter name (billing) | Primary telemetry fields | Required filters/dimensions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dedicated — Reserved capacity commit (monthly) | `DEDICATED_COMMIT` | N/A (contracted) | N/A (contract/CRM) | `deployment_mode='dedicated'` (for reporting only) | This is sourced from the contract/order (Finance system of record), not telemetry. Usage telemetry is used to explain burn-down dashboards but does not drive this line item unless explicitly contracted. |
| Dedicated — Included usage burn-down (reporting) | `DEDICATED_INCLUDED_USAGE` (not always invoiced) | `dedicated.text.total_tokens` (reporting) | `billed_input_tokens + billed_output_tokens` | `deployment_mode='dedicated'` | If this appears on an invoice (rare), confirm the contract specifies token-based included usage. Otherwise it should remain a Console/reporting construct only. |
| Dedicated — Overage usage | `DEDICATED_OVERAGE_TOKENS` | `dedicated.text.total_tokens` | `billed_input_tokens + billed_output_tokens` | `deployment_mode='dedicated'` AND contract overage flag | Ensure correct attribution to the dedicated pool (avoid double-counting when requests fail over to hosted fallback). |

**Dedicated attribution note:** A request should be tagged with `deployment_mode='dedicated'` only if it is served by the dedicated pool. Requests that are routed to hosted fallback (capacity constrained / policy fallback) must be billed as hosted unless the contract states otherwise. The authoritative indicator is the serving cluster tag recorded on the metering event.

---

## How to map common invoice segments (model/region/tier/endpoint)
Many invoices itemize usage by model and region for enterprise customers. When present, the line item description typically includes:
- Model label (e.g., “Llama 3.1 70B Instruct”)
- Region (e.g., “us-east-1”)
- Endpoint type (sometimes implicit: chat/completions vs embeddings/rerank)

### Canonical mapping rules
1) **Model shown on invoice** maps to `model_alias` at time of invoice run.
   - For reconciliation, prefer joining to the **model alias history table** (or the snapshot embedded in `invoice_usage_export`) so historical invoices don’t shift when aliases are renamed.
2) **Region shown on invoice** maps to `region` after normalization.
   - `us-east` (legacy) and `us-east-1` (canonical) should normalize to `us-east-1`.
3) **Endpoint type** is determined by the request route:
   - `/v1/chat/completions` → `endpoint_type='chat'`
   - `/v1/completions` → `endpoint_type='completions'`
   - `/v1/embeddings` → `endpoint_type='embeddings'`
   - `/v1/rerank` → `endpoint_type='rerank'`
4) **Customer tier** comes from the billing account snapshot at invoice-run time.
   - During plan migrations or experiments, use the tier snapshot attached to `invoice_run_id` rather than current CRM state.

---

## Worked examples

### Example A: Hosted text tokens itemized by model + region
**Invoice line items (simplified):**
1) Hosted API — Text generation: Input tokens (Model: `llama-3.1-70b`, Region: `us-east-1`) … 120,450,000 tokens
2) Hosted API — Text generation: Output tokens (Model: `llama-3.1-70b`, Region: `us-east-1`) … 31,220,000 tokens

**Telemetry filters to reproduce (invoice-run accurate):**
- Start from `invoice_usage_export` for the invoice’s `invoice_run_id`.
- Filter:
  - `deployment_mode='hosted'`
  - `endpoint_type IN ('chat','completions')`
  - `model_alias='llama-3.1-70b'` (or the invoice’s model label)
  - `region='us-east-1'`
- Sum fields:
  - Input line item: `SUM(billed_input_tokens)`
  - Output line item: `SUM(billed_output_tokens)`

**Expected match:** Exact match to invoice quantities (export is the invoice source). Differences vs Console are most commonly due to Console timezone display, alias mapping, or rounding display (see mismatch section).

---

### Example B: Embeddings units for batch calls
**Invoice line item:** Hosted API — Embeddings units … 2,340,000 units

**Telemetry interpretation:**
- `embedding_units` equals the number of individual texts/items embedded.
- If customer sent arrays of 32 items per request, the **request count** may be ~73,125 while **units** are 2,340,000.

**Reconcile tips:**
- Do not attempt to infer embedding units from token counts; use `embedding_units` directly.

---

### Example C: Streaming completion with client disconnect
**Invoice line item:** Hosted API — Text generation: Output tokens … X tokens

**Key rule (ADR-027):**
- We bill for output tokens **generated and delivered up to the point of disconnect**.
- We do **not** bill for tokens generated after the client disconnect is observed.

**What to check in telemetry:**
- Ensure metering events include `request_outcome` / streaming outcome fields where available.
- If investigating a known affected window, check whether the invoice was generated **pre- or post-backfill** for the streaming disconnect fix.

---

## Common mismatch causes and how to diagnose
These are the top reasons a customer’s Console usage and invoice line items may not match on first glance.

### 1) Time window alignment (UTC vs local)
**Symptom:** Console daily totals don’t match invoice period totals.
- Invoice aggregation windows are in **UTC** unless contractually specified otherwise.
- Console may display usage in the viewer’s locale/timezone.

**Diagnosis:** Compare using invoice period boundaries in UTC and/or use the invoice-run export.

### 2) Model alias changes over time
**Symptom:** Customer filters Console by a model name that doesn’t match the invoice label.
- Invoices use a snapshot of `model_alias` at invoice time.
- Console may show updated marketing names.

**Diagnosis:** Use alias history / invoice-run snapshot mapping.

### 3) Endpoint type confusion (chat vs completions)
**Symptom:** Customer believes all usage is “chat” but some traffic uses `/v1/completions`.

**Diagnosis:** Segment by `endpoint_type` and compare request routes.

### 4) Retries and replays
**Symptom:** Customer expects only “successful” requests to be billed; invoice includes higher-than-expected tokens.
- Some SDK/app patterns retry on network errors; depending on outcome, tokens may still be generated.
- Historically, missing retry dimensions could create confusion in breakdowns.

**Diagnosis:** Check `request_outcome` / `retry_reason` where available and compare with application logs. If a billing dispute is raised, follow the runbook intake template (request IDs, timestamps, and SDK retry config).

### 5) Streaming partials
**Symptom:** Customer thinks “it cut off, so it should be free.”
- Partial streaming responses can still deliver billable tokens.

**Diagnosis:** Verify delivered token counts up to disconnect and customer’s observed output.

### 6) Caching/batching misunderstandings
**Symptom:** Customer sees fewer model calls but is billed for many tokens.
- Continuous batching affects latency/cost but not token counts.
- Prefix caching may reduce compute cost; whether cached tokens are billed depends on plan configuration.

**Diagnosis:** Check whether `cached_input_tokens` is itemized (or rolled into input tokens) for that account/plan.

### 7) Backfills / meter-version changes
**Symptom:** Console numbers “changed” after an engineering fix, or invoice generated before a correction.

**Diagnosis:** Always anchor to `invoice_run_id`. If there’s a confirmed defect with customer impact, follow the discrepancy triage runbook and Finance approval flow for credits.

---

## Reconciliation checklist (for Finance/RevOps)
Use this before close sign-off when a sample is selected for reconciliation:
1) Identify the invoice’s `invoice_run_id` and billing period (UTC boundaries).
2) Pull line items and quantities from the invoice export.
3) Query `invoice_usage_export` grouped by `line_item_code`, `model_alias`, `region`, `endpoint_type`.
4) Confirm the export sums match line items exactly.
5) Compare export to `billing_usage_aggregates` for the same window and dimensions.
   - Expected tolerances and how to interpret deltas are defined on the Meter reconciliation methodology page.
6) If deltas exceed thresholds or indicate missing dimensions, open an issue with Telemetry/Metering and attach:
   - `invoice_run_id`
   - impacted `customer_id`
   - dimension breakdown
   - example request IDs (if available)

---

## Ownership and change control
**Owners:** Billing controls (Finance) + Metering pipelines (Engineering).

Any change that affects:
- line item naming,
- dimension inclusion/exclusion,
- model alias presentation,
- rounding/accounting,
- or what is considered billable for retries/streaming outcomes

…requires cross-functional sign-off from **Finance + Engineering + Legal** and must be documented (ADR or Confluence update) before rollout.

---

## Appendix: Field reference (billing export)
The invoice-run export contains (at minimum) the following columns used for auditability:
- `invoice_run_id`
- `customer_id`
- `line_item_code`
- `meter_name`
- `meter_version`
- `aggregation_window_start_utc`
- `aggregation_window_end_utc`
- `region`
- `endpoint_type`
- `model_id`
- `model_alias`
- `quantity`
- `unit` (tokens, units, requests)

If any of these columns are missing for a line item type, treat it as a defect for audit readiness and file a ticket.
